concept.name: Lee-Ready algorithm
concept.definition: The standard trade-classification procedure of Lee and Ready (1991) for inferring trade direction from intraday data: sign trades by the quote rule relative to the prevailing midpoint, sign midpoint trades by the tick rule, and match trades to quotes with an allowance for trade-reporting delay.
concept.intuition: Combine quote information with tick information to make the best guess about who initiated each trade.
concept.mechanics: Trades are aligned to the quotes in effect just before the report (a lag of roughly five seconds in their NYSE sample); prices above the midpoint are buys, below are sells, and midpoint trades inherit the sign of the last nonzero price change.
concept.failure_modes: Accuracy degrades in modern fast markets where quotes update far faster than trades are reported, for trades executed inside the spread, and for large or ECN-executed trades; validation studies on proprietary data find error rates around 20 percent in historical samples and higher in fast markets.
concept.misconceptions: Lee-Ready signs are estimates with material error rates, not ground truth about the aggressor; treating them as exact biases measures such as signed volume and price impact.
concept.example: A trade prints at the $50.005 midpoint after two consecutive upticks; Lee-Ready classifies it as buyer-initiated via the tick-test fallback.

citations.source: Lee and Ready, 'Inferring Trade Direction from Intraday Data', Journal of Finance 46(2):733-746 (course-hosted copy)
